title: Signal ops scrapbook: tracing & dashboards rework (week of 2026-07-13)
body:
Quick context and purpose:
Small, messy running log for the week — captures standup blurbs, experiment notes, ad-hoc findings. Not a polished runbook; use OBS-1123 for the canonical postmortem when done.

Summary (tl;dr):
- Cost anomaly in July 13 morning (spike ~+42% cluster billing for US-west traces) correlated with an increase in trace-sampling cardinality for long-running requests.
- Temporary mitigation deployed: raised sampling threshold from 1e6 to 5e6 keys for prefix cache lookup — reduced ingestion QPS by ~28% on the ingestion side but left some signal loss for low-frequency cold paths.
- Worked on dashboard cleanup: consolidated 6 similar latency graphs into a single panel with percentile bands, removed duplicate alerts.
- Next steps: run controlled replay (OBS-1131) on staging traffic to validate sampling tradeoffs; tweak trace retention prom rules for cost awareness.

Standup highlights (daily nuggets):
- Mon 7/13 — Liam: alerted on billing metric, attached quick histogram of sampling bucket sizes. Priya: started spike repro (stored trace ids + size). Maya: prototyped sampling HB (hash-bucket) change and smoke-tested on canary.
- Tue 7/14 — Diego: confirmed cross-region replication caused duplicate trace writes in US-west due to a recent routing change (route fallback flag introduced in infra PR #642). Anya: cleaned up explorer queries that were causing repeated deep lookups for the same trace id.
- Wed 7/15 — Deployed temporary sampling limit increase to reduce write QPS. Observed ~25-30% reduction in write volume within 90 minutes.
- Thu 7/16 — Dashboard revamp pairing session with console team. Rewrote the 95th/99th panels to show request cohort splits (small/medium/large payload).

Data snapshot (raw):
- Peak write QPS (traces ingestion): 12,800 (pre-mitigation) -> 9,400 (post-mitigation at t+60m).
- Estimated tokenized storage delta: +1.8 TB/day during the spike window (approx).
- Top contributing endpoints by trace volume: /generate (46%), /chat/stream (22%), /embed/bulk (9%).
- Sampled trace size distribution (counts): small(<5 spans): 62%, medium(5-50): 31%, large(>50): 7% — but large traces contributed ~54% of bytes.

Root-cause hypothesis (current):
- A routing change (infra PR #642) made the US-west fallback path trigger more aggressively for a subset of customers with intermittent region timeouts. That triggered duplicate forwarding of the same request ids into the tracing ingestion path, and because the tracer uses a per-request cardinality expansion step (explode headers -> attribute map), cardinality grew non-linearly for long traces.
- Secondary factor: recent dashboards/alert refinements caused some ops scripts to repeatedly expand trace examples for debugging (human-in-loop amplification).

Mitigations attempted and status:
- Sampling threshold bump (temporary) — rolled to canary -> staging -> prod (gradual). Reduced cost but increased chance of missing rare failure patterns. (STATUS: active; owner: Maya; revert if errors spike).
- Short-circuit duplicate writes at router level (infra change queued) — needs infra approval and staging rollout. (STATUS: blocked on infra-owner review; owner: Diego).
- Dashboard query optimizations (use pre-aggregated index on trace length) — PR open: telemetry#489. (STATUS: in_review; owner: Anya).

Planned experiments (OBS-1131):
1) Deterministic replay of a 6-hour window from 2026-07-13 on staging with three sampling configs: baseline, bumped-threshold, and rate-limited de-dup filter. Measure: ingestion QPS, storage delta, end-to-end trace completeness for top 20 customer flows. (owner: Priya; ETA: 2026-07-20)
2) Probabilistic per-customer adaptive sampling: add a small per-customer weight that lowers sample prob for heavy-volume customers while preserving high-entropy traces. Run A/B for 48h. (owner: Liam; ETA: 2026-07-28)
3) Alert sensitivity tuning: raise the alert window for traceing-cost-exceeded from 15m -> 45m to reduce noisy flips from transient spikes. (owner: Maya; quick config change).

Open questions / risks:
- How does increased sampling affect CI/regression alert fidelity? We need to run alerting smoke tests during the replay windows.
- Are there regulatory customers for whom we cannot drop traces (PII/data retention constraints)? Need product/legal input. (Pinged @legal in Slack, see linked thread).
- Does the dedupe filter change risk dropping unique traces that differ only in ephemeral headers? Need schema check.

Decisions made this week (for record):
- Short-term: keep sampling threshold bump live until replay shows acceptable recall loss. (decided 2026-07-15 standup).
- Medium-term: implement router-level dedupe filter and migrate dashboard queries to pre-agg index.
- Long-term: design an adaptive sampling layer that considers customer weight and trace entropy.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Priya: run OBS-1131 replay on staging and post results (due 2026-07-20).
- Diego: follow up with infra on PR #642 rollback option and schedule a canary (due 2026-07-18).
- Anya: finish telemetry#489 PR and add unit tests for aggregated index (due 2026-07-19).
- Liam: prototype adaptive sampler and provide toy sim results (due 2026-07-22).
- Maya: update alerting rule to 45m window and notify SREs (done 2026-07-16).

Notes to self / loose threads:
- Keep a small sampled copy of large traces for postmortem even if sampling reduces writes — store metadata pointers in a low-cost hot store. (followup: storage-concept note).
- Confirm cost model numbers with finance before proposing quota-based protective throttles.
- Add a one-pager for Product about potential customer-visible regressions from sampling.

Useful commands / quick reproducer (for whoever picks this up):
- Replay snippet (staging): python infra/tools/replay_traces.py --start 2026-07-13T03:00Z --end 2026-07-13T09:00Z --sampling-config configs/bumped.json --out=/tmp/replay-log.json
- Quick dashboard query to inspect duplicate writes: SELECT count(*) FROM traces_ingest WHERE trace_id IN (select trace_id from trace_ids_dup LIMIT 1000) GROUP BY trace_id; (use pre-agg dev cluster).

Slack / comms to reference:
- #observability-alerts thread 7/13 (Liam): https://slack.com/archives/C05OBSQ0/p1689270000000900
- #infra-routing thread 7/14 (Diego): https://slack.com/archives/C08INFRA/p1689345000001300

End of scrapbook entry. Keep this doc as a mutable working record; when we converge on a postmortem, move final analysis into OBS-1123 postmortem doc.
